summary.headline: Annu Projects Q2 FY27 revenue INR15.74 crore, PAT INR1.01 crore; H1 revenue INR35.65 crore with 19.64% EBITDA margin, H2-weighted business.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR15.74 crore with EBITDA of INR2.94 crore (18.68% margin) and PAT of INR1.01 crore, versus a loss before tax of INR3.48 crore in the year-ago quarter. H1 FY27 revenue rose to INR35.65 crore from INR6.51 crore in H1 FY26, with PAT of INR2.29 crore and EPS of INR0.45. Management attributed the weak Q2 versus Q1 to monsoon disruption and stated that the business is structurally weighted to H2. Order book stood at INR1,018 crore across 30 ongoing projects, with the BharatNet Kerala right-of-way approval still pending and holding back execution. Management guided to stronger Q3 and particularly Q4 but gave no numeric revenue guidance.

segments.name: Telecom infrastructure
segments.commentary: 81.23% of order book and the largest vertical; BharatNet Phase III Kerala is about INR741 crore of the order book, of which INR260 crore is AMC and only partly under execution.

segments.name: Sewerage infrastructure
segments.commentary: 14.65% of order book; management cited about INR100 crore of project work and about INR150 crore of AMC-type work, with regular AMC revenue of about INR50 crore a year.

segments.name: Railway signalling
segments.commentary: 2.49% of order book; new INR12.81 crore North East Frontier Railway OFC backbone contract spanning 143 km.

segments.name: Gas pipelines
segments.commentary: 1.63% of order book; no new revenue detail given beyond outlook commentary.

segments.name: Renewable energy (new)
segments.commentary: MoU with GEIE to supply materials for JVVNL rooftop solar, valued at INR44.3 crore, covering 8,000 systems in Dausa, Rajasthan under PM Surya Ghar; management is also negotiating a 100 MW turnkey opportunity.

guidance_outlook: Management declined numeric FY27 revenue guidance but said it is confident of maintaining the revenue growth CAGR of the last 3-4 years.
Margins expected to be sustained at the H1 level of about 19.6%, subject to right-of-way approvals, site handovers and certification timing.
Order book expected to reach around INR2,000 crore by year end (March 2027) under normal circumstances; Chairman later said by March end.
EPS expected to rise toward the FY26 level of INR6.91 as H2 execution picks up; Chairman said '100%' when asked if INR7 EPS is achievable this year.
Business momentum expected to strengthen in Q3 and be particularly strong in Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: IPO net proceeds about INR175.06 crore; INR20.5 crore for issue expenses, INR115 crore for working capital and INR15.4 crore for machinery. About INR70.3 crore utilised as of 30 September 2026, of which INR54.4 crore towards working capital.
Planned machinery purchase is HDD machines, used for existing work and for expansion into states where the company is not currently present.
Management said no additional capex or funding beyond IPO proceeds is required currently.
Kerala BharatNet: about INR260 crore AMC approved and partly executing; the remaining EPC portion (about INR500 crore) awaits DoT right-of-way approval.
Order-book execution profile: AMC projects over 6-10 years; EPC projects over 2-3 years.
demand_pricing: Bidding market is highly competitive and bidding margins are under pressure; management will not bid below internal margin thresholds.
Chairman said the company has bid for about INR3,000 crore of tenders and has been cleared on about 9.3% of them; an LOI of about INR125 crore is awaited this month.
Order inflow: L1 positions won in sewerage, gas and railways, not disclosed pending LOA.

Demand drivers cited: data-centre fibre demand (hyperscalers), gas share of energy mix rising from 6% to 15% by FY30, and sewerage treatment gap (only 28% of sewage treated; wastewater market to reach INR378.10 billion by FY30).
Order book composition: about 81% telecom, so FY27 revenue largely telecom-driven per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5.7x H1 revenue growth sustainable and can similar growth continue?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said revenue is H2-weighted due to project awards and execution, and the company is confident of maintaining current revenue run-rate, without quantifying.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue fall sequentially from about INR20 crore in Q1 to about INR15-16 crore in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Monsoon halted trenching and site work in Q2, so milestones could not be completed or billed; EPC revenue is concentrated in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the share price decline reflecting fundamentals?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO declined to comment on the share price, said IPO was transparently disclosed and that results will show fundamentals in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the sustainable margins and what could move them?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects H1 margin of about 19.6% to be sustained; key risks are right-of-way approvals, land, site handovers and measurement/certification delays.

qa_highlights.question: Can EPS reach INR7 this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 EPS is INR0.45, not INR2; FY26 EPS was INR6.91; Chairman said 100% that the INR7 mark can be reached as H2 execution lands.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline and status of BharatNet Kerala project?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said about INR800 crore Kerala order includes INR260 crore AMC over 10 years; EPC of about INR500 crore starts only after DoT right-of-way approval, which management hopes is imminent.

qa_highlights.question: How will IPO proceeds and capex be used, and is more funding needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Proceeds of INR175.06 crore: INR115 crore working capital and INR15.4 crore machinery (HDD machines); about INR70.3 crore used by 30 September; no further funding currently required.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables fell to INR142 crore from INR156 crore and unbilled to INR59 crore from INR76 crore since March; receivable days down to 192 from 237; about INR73 crore collected from prior year.

risks_watch: BharatNet Kerala EPC (about INR500-520 crore) remains blocked until DoT right-of-way approvals are received; timing is uncertain.
Revenue is heavily H2-weighted; Q1 and Q2 are seasonally weak, so FY27 full-year delivery depends on Q3/Q4 milestone billing.
Receivables of INR142 crore and receivable days of 192 remain high relative to revenue; collection must keep pace with execution.
Competitive bidding pressure; management says it will not bid below margin thresholds, which may limit order inflows against the INR2,000 crore year-end target.
Share price weakness after listing and investor concern about communication; management declined to comment on share price.
Expansion into renewable energy (solar supply, 100 MW turnkey) and railway OFC is early-stage and not yet material.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and H2 ramp-up, but evasive on specifics: declined numeric FY27 revenue guidance and share price questions, and relied on seasonality and approval timing to explain weak H1. Defensive when challenged by investors on communication after the IPO.
key_quotes: We will not go below our internal margin threshold merely to add to the order book.
As execution progresses across our key projects and the required approvals are received, we expect business momentum to strengthen in Q3 and be particularly strong in Q4 of FY27.
Our true measure of success would lie in the operational execution of our work.
If you have completed your 99% of the job and 1% is left out then you cannot bill your revenue.

adds.what: HDD machines for existing work and expansion into new states (no count or capex stated beyond INR15.4 crore machinery allocation from IPO proceeds)

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management is confident of sustaining the 3-4 year revenue CAGR, targets an order book of about INR2,000 crore by March 2027 and a 19.6% margin, with EPS toward INR6.91-7 questioned but affirmed by the Chairman; backing is a INR1,018 crore order book and a pending INR125 crore LOI, but Kerala BharatNet ROW approval is still pending.

oneOffs.what: Q2 FY26 loss before tax of INR3.48 crore and total income of INR3.70 crore versus INR16.54 crore in Q2 FY27 make the YoY comparison very weak-based; H1 FY26 revenue was only INR6.51 crore
Q2 FY27 PAT of INR1.01 crore includes INR0.80 crore other income against EBITDA of INR2.94 crore

quality.why: Reported YoY growth is driven mainly by a very weak year-ago base (Q2 FY26 loss before tax INR3.48 crore, H1 FY26 revenue INR6.51 crore) rather than a demonstrated recurring run-rate; Q2 FY27 revenue of INR15.74 crore was down sequentially from about INR20 crore in Q1 on monsoon disruption, and the brief gives no volume figure or YoY revenue number for Q2.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects the H1 EBITDA margin of about 19.6% to be sustained (vs 18.68% in Q2 alone), subject to right-of-way approvals, site handovers and certification timing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: IPO proceeds of INR15.4 crore are earmarked for HDD machines to serve existing work and new states, but no count, capex or commissioning date is given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book of INR1,018 crore across 30 projects and a 5.7x H1 revenue jump (INR35.65 crore vs INR6.51 crore), with management expecting Q3 and especially Q4 to be stronger; execution is contingent on BharatNet Kerala ROW approval.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said no additional capex or funding beyond IPO proceeds (about INR175 crore, of which about INR70.3 crore used by 30 Sep 2026) is required currently.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric revenue guidance was given, and bidding margins are under pressure with management refusing to bid below internal thresholds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 delivery is H2-loaded and about INR500 crore of BharatNet Kerala EPC awaits DoT right-of-way approval with no firm timing, while Q1 and Q2 were weak (about INR20 crore then about INR15.7 crore).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Renewable energy (INR44.3 crore rooftop solar MoU for 8,000 systems in Dausa) and a 100 MW turnkey opportunity under negotiation are early-stage and not yet material.

rows.label: Order book to about INR2,000 crore by March 2027
rows.why: Order book is INR1,018 crore and management targets about INR2,000 crore, but a pending INR125 crore LOI and tight bidding margins (about 9.3% of INR3,000 crore bids cleared) make it conditional.

rows.label: Receivable days falling from 237 to 192
rows.why: Trade receivables fell to INR142 crore from INR156 crore and unbilled revenue to INR59 crore from INR76 crore since March 2026, though 192 days remains high.

rows.label: DoT right-of-way approval for BharatNet Kerala EPC
rows.why: The roughly INR500 crore EPC portion is blocked until approval; management hopes it is imminent but gave no date.

tone.note: Management was confident about the H2 ramp, the 19.6% margin and the INR2,000 crore order-book target, but evasive on numeric guidance and share price, and defensive on IPO communication. Analysts pushed on the sequential revenue decline, EPS reaching INR7, and BharatNet approvals.
